title: Life and Adventure in Japan

divisions.title: The book’s title above Chapter I

summary: An American teacher’s account of four years in the service of the Japanese government, 1871–75, written for young readers and, as the preface says, “from a Christian standpoint.” Clark travels from Yokohama along the Tokaido to Shizuoka (“Shidz-u-o-ka”), the town of the retired shogun, where he teaches for two years, living first in a Buddhist temple and then in a new house in the grounds of the old castle. He describes his excursions, the ascent of Mount Fuji, and the making of tea.

He then moves to Tokyo to teach at the Kaisei Gakko, the government college, and writes of the capital, a visit to the emperor’s palace, and a journey to Kyoto, ending with the prospects of Christian missions in Japan. The book has thirty engravings from photographs and a map.
omitted_from_reading: The printed contents, the list of illustrations, and the book’s title above Chapter I are in the JSON only.
